Part 2&3 物品 OBJECTS

Describe a piece of technology (not a phone) that you would like to own

描述一件你想拥有的科技产品(非手机)

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a piece of technology (not a phone) that you would like to own

  • What it is (它是什么)
  • How much it costs (它多少钱)
  • How you knew it (你是怎么知道它的)
  • And explain why you would like to own it (并解释为什么你想拥有它)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a piece of technology (not a phone) that you would like to own

The piece of technology I'd love to own is a 3D printer. For those who don't know, it's a machine that builds physical objects layer by layer from digital designs, using materials like plastic filament. You can print anything from small toys to replacement parts for household items. In terms of price, a decent entry-level 3D printer costs around two to three thousand yuan, which is not cheap, but it's affordable enough for a hobby. The higher-end models can cost much more, but I think a basic one would be enough for me to start with. I first learned about 3D printers a few years ago from videos online. I remember watching a creator print a fully working mechanical gear, and I was amazed that a machine at home could produce something so precise. Since then, I've followed quite a few makers on Bilibili who share their printing projects. The main reason I want one is that I'd like to experience hands-on making. I've always been curious about how things are built, and a 3D printer would let me turn my own ideas into real objects. I mean, there's a big difference between looking at a design on a screen and actually holding the finished product in your hand. So for me, it's not just a gadget, it's a way to learn and create.

我想拥有一台3D打印机，入门款大概两三千元；几年前在网上看到有人打印出精密齿轮，从此关注了很多B站创作者的打印项目；想亲手把想法变成实物，体验动手创造的乐趣。

Q2What are the differences between the technology of the past and that of today?

I think the biggest difference is speed and connectivity. In the past, technology was mostly mechanical and slow, for example, people communicated through letters that took days to arrive. Today, everything is digital and instant, we can video call someone on the other side of the world in seconds. Also, modern technology is much smaller and more portable, a smartphone today has more power than computers from thirty years ago. I'd say the pace of change itself is also a difference, technology now updates almost every year.

过去机械、慢（信件要几天），现在数字、即时（视频通话秒连）；现代设备更小更便携，更新换代更快。

Q3What technology do young people like to use?

Young people are usually drawn to technology that is fast, visual and social. Smartphones are obviously the most essential, since they combine communication, entertainment and work in one device. Beyond that, many young people enjoy gaming consoles, wireless earphones and smartwatches, which fit their active lifestyles. Social media apps are also a big part of their daily routine. I think the common thread is convenience, young people prefer technology that saves time and connects them with others instantly.

年轻人爱快、视觉化、社交化的科技：手机最核心，还有游戏机、无线耳机、智能手表；共同点是方便、即时连接。

Q4What are the differences between online and face-to-face communication?

I think the main difference is the level of emotional connection. Face-to-face communication includes body language, eye contact and tone of voice, which help people understand each other more deeply. Online communication, on the other hand, is more convenient and efficient, especially for long-distance relationships or work meetings. However, it can easily lead to misunderstandings, because text messages lack emotion. So I'd say face-to-face is warmer and more genuine, while online is faster and more practical, and both have their place in modern life.

面对面有肢体语言和语气，情感更深；线上方便高效但容易误解；面对面更温暖，线上更实用。

Q5Do you think technology has changed the way people communicate?

Definitely, I think technology has transformed communication completely. In the past, people mainly communicated face to face or through letters, which took time and effort. Nowadays, we send messages, share photos and make video calls instantly, and we can stay in touch with people across the world. I think this has made communication more frequent but also more casual, for example, people now send quick messages instead of writing long letters. Having said that, I believe the quality of deep conversations hasn't improved, and might even have declined.

彻底改变了：从面对面/信件到即时消息和视频通话；交流更频繁但更随意，深度对话反而可能变少。

Q6What negative effects does technology have on people's relationships?

I think there are several negative effects. Firstly, people spend so much time on their phones that they sometimes ignore the people physically around them, which weakens family bonds. Secondly, online communication can create misunderstandings, because it's hard to read emotions through text. Also, social media sometimes causes jealousy or comparison, which puts pressure on relationships. That said, I don't think technology itself is the problem, it's how people use it. If used wisely, it can actually strengthen relationships by keeping people connected.

沉迷手机忽略身边人、文字交流易误解、社交媒体引发攀比；但问题在用法不在技术本身。

Q7What are the differences between making friends in real life and online?

I think the biggest difference is depth. Friends made in real life usually develop trust gradually through shared experiences, like studying together or playing sports, so the bond tends to be stronger. Online friendships, in contrast, are often based on common interests and can form very quickly, but they may stay superficial. Also, real-life friends can offer practical support, while online friends mainly provide emotional company. Having said that, online friendships can become real ones if people eventually meet, so I'd say both types have value.

现实友谊靠共同经历建立信任，更深；网上友谊基于共同兴趣、来得快但可能浅；网上友谊见面后也能变真。
